Tesla (TSLA) closed at $378.03 in the latest trading session, marking a -1.22% move from the prior day. The stock's performance was behind the S&P 500's daily loss of 0.06%. Meanwhile, the Dow gained 0.38%, and the Nasdaq, a tech-heavy index, lost 0.44%.

The electric car maker's shares have seen an increase of 4.72% over the last month, surpassing the Auto-Tires-Trucks sector's gain of 0.28% and the S&P 500's gain of 2.36%.

Investors will be eagerly watching for the performance of Tesla in its upcoming earnings disclosure. The company's earnings report is set to be unveiled on October 21, 2026. In that report, analysts expect Tesla to post earnings of $0.44 per share. This would mark a year-over-year decline of 12%. Our most recent consensus estimate is calling for quarterly revenue of $27.8 billion, down 1.03% from the year-ago period.

For the entire fiscal year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates are projecting earnings of $1.7 per share and a revenue of $105.96 billion, representing changes of +2.41% and +11.74%, respectively, from the prior year.

Investors should also note any recent changes to analyst estimates for Tesla. Such recent modifications usually signify the changing landscape of near-term business trends. Consequently, upward revisions in estimates express analysts' positivity towards the business operations and its ability to generate profits.

Empirical research indicates that these revisions in estimates have a direct correlation with impending stock price performance. We developed the Zacks Rank to capitalize on this phenomenon. Our system takes these estimate changes into account and delivers a clear, actionable rating model.

Ranging from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), the Zacks Rank system has a proven, outside-audited track record of outperformance, with #1 stocks returning an average of +25% annually since 1988. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate has witnessed a 14.2% decrease. Right now, Tesla possesses a Zacks Rank of #4 (Sell).

Valuation is also important, so investors should note that Tesla has a Forward P/E ratio of 224.87 right now. This expresses a premium compared to the average Forward P/E of 16.04 of its industry.

Meanwhile, TSLA's PEG ratio is currently 10.11. The PEG ratio bears resemblance to the frequently used P/E ratio, but this parameter also includes the company's expected earnings growth trajectory. The Automotive - Domestic industry had an average PEG ratio of 0.93 as trading concluded yesterday.

The Automotive - Domestic industry is part of the Auto-Tires-Trucks sector. Currently, this industry holds a Zacks Industry Rank of 82, positioning it in the top 34% of all 250+ industries.

title: Tesla Faces New Luxury EV Rival in France as Lucid Plans 16 Locations
detail:
Tesla Faces New Luxury EV Rival in France as Lucid Plans 16 Locations
The rear of a dark car features the chrome LUCID logo embedded in a horizontal red light bar. (Credit: Image via Shutterstock)

Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Lucid Group, Inc. is taking a new step into Europe's luxury electric vehicle market, with France set to become a larger part of its retail strategy in 2027.

The expansion gives Tesla Inc. another premium EV competitor to watch, though Lucid's challenge is not just winning customers — it is building a service network and converting high-end interest into sustained deliveries.

Lucid Targets France in 2027

Lucid plans to open its first three retail and service locations in France in the first quarter of 2027, with more than 16 partner locations targeted by the end of that year. The company announced the rollout on Oct. 12, naming Emil Frey France as its partner.

The planned locations will allow customers to experience and order both the Lucid Air sedan and Gravity SUV. Reservations with priority for future ordering are already available through Lucid's French website, while orders are expected to open in the first quarter of 2027.

The company advertises up to 960 kilometers of WLTP range for the Air and up to 739 kilometers for the Gravity. The Gravity also offers seating for up to seven, giving Lucid a larger SUV to pitch to buyers who want luxury, space and electric performance.

France is an attractive market to target. Electric vehicles accounted for 42% of new car registrations in September, according to Reuters.

Tesla Has the Established Network

Tesla already has a substantial footprint in France, with stores and service centers listed across major regions on its official French locations page.

Lucid's partnership with Emil Frey France gives it a route to expand through an established automotive retail network rather than relying entirely on company-operated sites.

See Also: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time

For Tesla, the competitive question is whether Lucid can turn its product specifications into a credible alternative for buyers considering high-end electric sedans and SUVs. France's growing EV market creates an opportunity, but Tesla's existing presence gives it a head start.

Lucid's Execution Test

The expansion also comes as Lucid works through a more immediate challenge: scaling demand and deliveries.

The company delivered 3,806 vehicles in the third quarter of 2026, below the average analyst estimate of 4,687. Production fell to 2,954 vehicles as Lucid reduced output and worked through inventory under a cost-cutting plan.

Analysts Raise Targets on Securitize, Coinbase, Robinhood; BofA Cuts eToro

StoneX raised its price target on Securitize (NYSE: $SECZ) by 50% on Monday, adding to a run of target changes on crypto-linked stocks this month ahead of third-quarter earnings.

StoneX analyst Mark Palmer lifted his target to $18 from $12 and kept a Buy rating. He argued that Securitize's new tokenized stock trading platform, launched last Thursday, will open a major new revenue stream. Shares fell about 10% Monday morning, leaving the new target roughly 45% above current prices. Palmer said the market still values Securitize like a tokenization vendor, even though it now operates as a market.

Management said on its August earnings call that most tokenization revenue came from integration fees, meaning little of the $5.3 billion in second-quarter transaction volume was monetized, according to StoneX. The new platform lets the company earn fees on transactions and servicing, with possible collateral revenue later. Last week's launch put stocks including Apple (NASDAQ: $AAPL), Nvidia (NASDAQ: $NVDA) and Tesla (NASDAQ: $TSLA) on Solana, backed one-for-one by underlying shares and settling in USDC (CRYPTO: $USDC).

StoneX projects revenue of nearly $120 million in 2027 and almost $200 million in 2028, about 65% annual growth. Its $18 target implies a 14.5-times enterprise-value-to-revenue multiple on the 2028 forecast.

Bank of America (NYSE: $BAC) analyst Craig Siegenthaler made his own moves on Oct. 5. He raised Robinhood (NASDAQ: $HOOD) to $156 from $140 and Coinbase (NASDAQ: $COIN) to $203 from $174, keeping Buy ratings on both. He cut eToro (NASDAQ: $ETOR) to $39 from $46 with a Neutral rating.

Expectations differ by company. Robinhood is expected to report third-quarter earnings of $0.64 per share on revenue near $1.4 billion, and has beaten EPS estimates in each of its last 11 quarters. Coinbase is projected to post a $0.20 per-share loss on about $1.77 billion in revenue, after missing estimates in each of the last three quarters. eToro is forecast at $0.40 per share on roughly $203 million.

Commentary tied the Coinbase increase partly to expected stablecoin revenue after the Federal Reserve's September rate increase, even as near-term trading volume forecasts were trimmed.

detail:
Rivian Automotive (RIVN) vs. TSLA and F: Can Improving Margins and Its R2 Midsize SUV Unlock Profitable Growth?
Ricardo Pillai

Is RIVN a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Rivian Automotive, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on RIVN. Rivian Automotive, Inc.'s share was trading at $13.96 as of October 9th 2026.

This isn't the first time we see an automaker pitched as a great investment. Unfortunately, RIVN shares lost 29.17% of their value year to date. Comparable stocks like Ford Motor Company (F) lost 7.24% of their value during the same period. Why are auto stocks declining so much and is it really a good time to buy them?

Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile (SQM) PT Raised to $100 at Scotiabank as Top 2026 Pick

In April, we published an article about the 10 Best Car Stocks to Buy in 2026 and RIVN ranked #4 in that article. Unfortunately, RIVN has lost 6.55% since then, likely reflecting concerns about cash burn, share dilution, and weaker EV demand. This article explains why TD Cowen, an investment banking firm within TD Securities, also turned bullish on RIVN ahead of the R2 launch. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Rivian Automotive, Inc. (NASDAQ:RIVN) designs and builds electric vehicles, including the R1T pickup, R1S SUV, commercial vans, and its newly launched R2 midsize SUV, along with the software, charging, fleet management, and autonomous-driving technology that support them. Its central investment case right now is the R2 platform, and that's key to understanding whether Rivian can turn years of heavy manufacturing investment into a scalable, higher-volume EV business.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

The roughly $45,000 R2 began customer deliveries in June 2026 and was built for lower costs, simpler assembly, and higher production volumes. In the second quarter of 2026, revenue grew about 27% year over year to $1.7 billion, and Rivian posted a record $179 million in quarterly gross profit, marking four straight quarters of positive gross margin. That's real progress, but the company still lost $2.58 per share on a trailing basis, and its stock trades at close to 3.7 times trailing sales — a sign that investors are paying less for what Rivian earns today and more for what they expect the R2 ramp to deliver in profits and cash flow down the road.

The bullish case for Rivian Automotive rests on the idea that higher R2 production volumes and its lower-cost design can steadily improve the company's unit economics. Rivian absorbed about $100 million in one-time costs tied to ramping up R2 production, while its software and services business brought in $515 million of second-quarter revenue at a strong 42% gross margin, generating $215 million in profit that helped offset a $36 million loss on the automotive side. Management is aiming for positive per-unit gross margins on the R2 by the end of 2026, so how quickly the platform can scale while cutting manufacturing costs is central to the turnaround story.

Tesla (TSLA) and other US auto original equipment manufacturers, excluding Rivian Automotive (RIVN) and Lucid Group (LCID), are expected to benefit from pricing power and higher average transaction prices heading into earnings, driven by a resilient seasonally adjusted annual rate, or SAAR, RBC Capital Markets said in a note emailed Monday.

General Motors (GM) and Ford Motor (F) could see "meaningful" upside from a potential US-Mexico bilateral trade agreement before the end of the year, RBC analysts said.

Despite negative investor sentiment, the analysts said that Tesla's risk-reward profile leans positive, with Q3 deliveries surpassing consensus estimates, while the Q3 consensus on automotive gross margins excluding regulatory credits are "reasonable."

Meanwhile, General Motors is well-positioned to surpass its pricing growth target of 0.5% for 2026, supported by the steady SAAR environment in the US, the analysts said. They added that the company's 2027 outlook remains "compelling," with profit growth driven by Gen 6 truck platform contributions and narrowing EV losses, among other factors.

RBC maintained its rating on General Motors' stock at outperform and raised the price target to $102 from $100. The brokerage kept Tesla's stock rating at outperform with a price target of $480 and Ford at sector-perform with a price target of $15.

title: Jefferies raises Tesla price target as resilient deliveries support automotive outlook
detail:
Jefferies raises Tesla price target as resilient deliveries support automotive outlook
Proactive

TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Jefferies raises Tesla price target as resilient deliveries support automotive outlook Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Jefferies has raised its price target for Tesla Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA), the electric carmaker, to $400 from $350, as resilient vehicle deliveries and improving prospects for non-automotive businesses offset concerns over rising investment and operating costs.

Analyst Philippe Houchois maintained a 'hold' rating, with the revised target implying 5% upside from Tesla's closing price of $382.70 cited in the 12 October research note.

Jefferies expects third-quarter revenue of $29.2 billion, an automotive gross margin of 16.7% and adjusted operating profit of $781 million, while forecasting cash outflow of about $5 billion.

Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles during the quarter, up 1% from the previous three months but down 2% year on year, with its Model 3 and Model Y accounting for 478,200 deliveries.

The broker said demand across China, Europe and the United States had proved resilient, reflecting Tesla's competitive value for money as well as lower comparison figures in some markets and higher fuel costs in Europe.

Production reached 464,400 vehicles, leaving output below deliveries, although Jefferies expects year-to-date production and deliveries to remain broadly aligned and support working capital.

The broker forecast automotive revenue of $21 billion, with a limited contribution of $140 million from regulatory credits, while stronger software uptake and improved vehicle resale values could support margins.

However, sustained research and development and selling costs are expected to weigh on profitability, while capital expenditure of $8 billion underpins Jefferies' forecast of substantial cash outflow.

Jefferies has cut longer-term estimates because of the limited range of new vehicle models, slower energy-storage growth and the likelihood that newer ventures will initially generate losses.

The bank nevertheless sees improving prospects for full self-driving software, energy storage and robotaxis, while Tesla's semi-truck programme is moving into production despite limited visibility over orders.

Houchois also highlighted the possibility of a future merger with SpaceX Corp (NASDAQ:SPCX), arguing that overlapping technology ambitions, investment requirements and Elon Musk's preference for retaining control could strengthen the strategic case.

The price-target increase therefore reflects potential value from Tesla's broader technology ambitions rather than a clear improvement in its near-term earnings outlook.
